package.title: Authorization Package
package.note: Structured like a System Security Plan. Every statement cites its source; outcome figures are as reported in the résumé, not live telemetry.

subject.name: Sai Vignesh Rayal

I design access so there is nothing to steal, write the controls as code, and keep the evidence that proves they hold.

controls.name: Identity & Access
controls.statement: Workload access built so no reusable credential exists.

implementation.text: Managed identity scoped to Key Vault Secrets User on exactly one secret; a decoy secret proves the boundary with a 403.
Secretless CI/CD through GitHub OIDC, with an ABAC condition limiting which role the pipeline can grant.
Access-control reviews; cloud solutions integrated securely while supporting researcher access needs.

controls.name: Cloud Boundary & Configuration
controls.statement: Networks default-deny; configuration is code and is tested before it exists.

implementation.text: Key Vault reachable only from the workload subnet; 31 tests run against the compiled template before deploy.
Sealed AWS lab network: no internet gateway, no NAT, no public IPs, quarantine subnet, guardrail tests in CI.
Secured Azure VMs, networking and storage while reducing infrastructure cost 15%.
Designed AWS architectures on EC2, EKS, VPC, S3 and RDS with security controls, load balancing and auto-scaling.

controls.name: Risk & Assessment
controls.statement: Find the misconfiguration before an attacker does, and write down what remains.

implementation.text: Vulnerability testing and security assessments across infrastructure, access and configuration — high-risk misconfiguration exposure down 25%.
STRIDE threat model (T01–T15), eight adversary-emulation scenarios, findings fixed and re-tested or formally risk-accepted.

controls.name: Detection & Response
controls.statement: Every read, denial and permission change is logged, alerted and rehearsed.

implementation.text: KQL hunts for secret reads, denials, unexpected networks, RBAC changes and log tampering; incident runbooks for token theft and escalation.
Monitored cloud systems for irregular behaviour and supported triage, containment and remediation — response turnaround 20% faster.
VPC flow logs on all traffic to encrypted storage; sensor subnet reserved for Zeek and Suricata.

controls.name: DevSecOps & Supply Chain
controls.statement: The pipeline is a security control, not a delivery convenience.

implementation.text: CI runs Bicep lint with security rules as errors, Checkov, Gitleaks over full history and traceability tests.
Terraform and PowerShell provisioning — manual effort down 40%, deployments consistent.
Azure administration automated with PowerShell and JSON templates — manual effort down 30%.

controls.name: Data Protection & Endpoint
controls.statement: Regulated data stays classified, contained and on compliant devices.

implementation.text: Microsoft Security & Compliance Center policies — DLP and threat-management controls — and Defender across Microsoft 365.
Intune and SCCM across 500+ devices: compliance enforcement, patching, device policy — security incidents down 25%.

controls.name: Governance, Risk & Compliance
controls.statement: Controls are mapped, traceable, and a build fails if a threat loses its control.

implementation.text: Security requirements and control mappings for healthcare and research platforms — documented control coverage up 35%.
29 NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls mapped to implementation, test, evidence and threat; crosswalk to CSF 2.0, SP 800-207, CIS and MCSB.
Standards, runbooks, continuity and disaster-recovery procedures — audit readiness and resilience up 30%; HIPAA-aligned and NIST-based practice.
Backup and DR for Azure resources and SQL databases supporting 99.9% availability.

layers.title: Identity
layers.question: Who may enter.
layers.scene: Only verified identities pass the gate. Everything else stops before it reaches the network.

layers.title: Network
layers.question: Where it may go.
layers.scene: Four subnets and no route out. Quarantine can only talk to the sensors.

layers.title: Workload
layers.question: What it may run.
layers.scene: Probed from inside the workload: one action allowed, seven denied.

layers.title: Data
layers.question: What it may read.
layers.scene: One identity, one secret, one network path to it.

layers.title: Detection
layers.question: What we will see.
layers.scene: Every read, denial and permission change is logged and alerted.

layers.title: Evidence
layers.question: Proof that it held.
layers.scene: Controls mapped to tests, tests to evidence, evidence hashed.
